description: For unary \(P\), a constant \(a\), and the ground substitution sending every variable to \(a\), the clause \(\{P(x_0),P(x_1)\}\) has image \(\{P(a)\}\); deleting either one of its two literals before substitution still leaves that same nonempty ground image.
signature:
Lemmatheca.Entry.FirstOrderResolution.duplicate_pivot_fiber.{u, v} {L : FirstOrder.Language} (P : L.Relations 1)
  (a : L.Functions 0) :
  have γ := fun x => Lemmatheca.Entry.FirstOrderResolution.constant a;
  have p := Lemmatheca.Entry.FirstOrderResolution.unaryAtom P (Lemmatheca.Entry.FirstOrderResolution.constant a);
  Lemmatheca.MathematicalLogic.HerbrandModels.clauseSubst γ (Lemmatheca.Entry.FirstOrderResolution.pairPositive P) =
      {Lemmatheca.Entry.FirstOrderResolution.signed true p} ∧
    Lemmatheca.MathematicalLogic.HerbrandModels.clauseSubst γ
          (Finset.erase (Lemmatheca.Entry.FirstOrderResolution.pairPositive P)
            (Lemmatheca.Entry.FirstOrderResolution.signed true
              (Lemmatheca.Entry.FirstOrderResolution.unaryAtom P (FirstOrder.Language.var 0)))) =
        {Lemmatheca.Entry.FirstOrderResolution.signed true p} ∧
      Lemmatheca.MathematicalLogic.HerbrandModels.clauseSubst γ
          (Finset.erase (Lemmatheca.Entry.FirstOrderResolution.pairPositive P)
            (Lemmatheca.Entry.FirstOrderResolution.signed true
              (Lemmatheca.Entry.FirstOrderResolution.unaryAtom P (FirstOrder.Language.var 1)))) =
        {Lemmatheca.Entry.FirstOrderResolution.signed true p}
